row.name: Direct East Face
row.overview: Pass Midnight Lake on its right, hike toward Blue Heaven Lake, then contour west past small tarns. The line follows a bowl flanked by two ribs, starting right of the snow high point: easy corner crack, traverse beneath an overhang leftward (5.6) to a ledge. A chockstone at its back left is overhanging: bouldery, maybe hard 5.9 or 10a, 5ft long; gear may be pulled. Then roughly 200 feet more of easy fifth class. On loose lower-angle ground swap into approach shoes and scramble up the gully to the notch under the summit spire. From there, take a ledge down right, a smooth chimney, a ledge round to the Southeast, then a corner crack that offers solid jams, and mantle.
row.approach: Go around Midnight Lake on its right, climb toward Blue Heaven Lake, then contour west past small unnamed lakes to the base of the broad east face. The route starts in the recess marked by a dark water stain, in the middle of the face.

row.name: Christine
row.overview: Granite cracks, mostly hands, lead directly up the "Lamorck" sub peak to its summit in four pitches graded 5.8, 5.9, 5.9+ and 5.9+ (40m, 25m, 55m, 25m). The 55m pitch passes a roof and may be split in two. Twin cracks finish at the ridge.
row.approach: From North Lake, walk the Lamarck Lakes trail up as far as the upper lake. Where it forks, bear left and cross the creek, then leave the main trail about a hundred yards beyond it. Head across the hills left of the lake toward the subpeak that holds the Ladies wall, following cairns to a boulder field, and pick the easiest line through the boulders to the foot of the crag.
row.descent_text: From the top, either walk off or rappel. For the walk-off, go left (south and southeast) over third and fourth class ground to the high point of the ridge, then trend down and left along ledges to easier ground. From there, join the Lamarck Col trail or contour beneath the wall over talus and gravel back to the base. In early season the contour can be snow-covered. The rappel option starts from an anchor on the ridge a short way south of the top and runs down the wall to the base.

row.name: Standard route
row.description: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 5.

row.name: West Gully to North Ridge
row.description: Reach the Evolution Meadow area via the John Muir Trail, then climb the broad west-face gully to the north ridge and follow it to the top. Rock is loose; exit the gully to the south after the second tower to avoid class 3.

row.name: West Ridge
row.description: Follow the trail past Post Corral Creek to Fleming and Lower Indian lakes, then go cross-country up grassy slopes to the west ridge and along it to the top. About 2 miles and 2,000 ft past the lake.

row.name: North Central Couloir
row.overview: The central of three prominent north-face couloirs between the saddle and the lower western summit, and the steepest and narrowest. The bergschrund at its foot, a big one, is probably the crux. Easy mixed ground on the left leads out of it to an ice wall of about 15 feet capped by an overhanging lip; a harder chimney between rock and snow may exist on the right. Above, the gully narrows and steepens to 55-60 degrees, with one or two simple boulder moves at the blocks high up. Short for the long approach.
row.approach: Hike over Piute Pass from the North Lake trailhead, then turn left shortly after the pass toward Muriel Lake and skirt its east side. The next stretch crosses rugged boulder-strewn shorelines and talus to the Goethe Glacier, from which the north-side couloirs rise.
